outcome.technical:
tools/gate-parity.py: new section 'how many jobs one run asks GitHub for at once' - JOB_CAP = 20 with its basis in a comment (GitHub's documented Free-plan figure as the finding states it, plus the measurement ci.yml's lint-job comment records: release-tier runs of twenty-two jobs, exactly two started late; the cap is the account's, so the count is one run's least ask, not a promise). concurrent_jobs(text) counts per tier (per-run, release) each job's matrix cells via _matrix_cells (after exclude/include), on the tiers _if_tier reaches (an unproved condition is counted on both); a job tied by `needs` (transitively, either direction) to every other job of its tier runs alone and is listed in `alone`, not counted (this is `verified` on both tiers); every other job is counted as concurrent - an over-count when a deeper needs-chain keeps two apart, never an under-count, said in the docstring. Unreadable matrix, block-form `needs`, `needs` naming no job, and no jobs block are each findings. job_cap_drift(text, cap=JOB_CAP) reports '<tier> tier' over the cap with count, per-job breakdown, cap, and the excess. job_cap_verdict(repo) wires it into parity() as key 'job_cap' (unreadable ci.yml is a finding); render() prints 'CI job cap (<tier>)' and the clean sentence names the rule; module docstring bullet added; WINDOWS_SHARDS comment says job_cap_drift holds the linux count. Cases: jc0 live claim (real ci.yml: per-run 16 = selftests 12 + e2e + lint + browser-panel + browser-report, release 17 with resample, alone == ['verified'] both tiers, findings []); jc1 one over the cap (21) names both tiers with 21 and 20 in the why; jc2 ALLOW exactly at cap (20) behind a needs-gated verified is clean, alone == ['verified']; jc3 a release-only job past the cap names the release tier alone, in a fixture and in the live ci.yml with resample given a matrix of the cap's size; jc4 a job needing nothing beside the gate makes the gate counted (alone == []); jc5 block-form needs / unknown needs / unresolvable matrix / no jobs each a single named finding. sv20 and sv9 extended with 'job_cap'. gate-parity --selftest 119/119 (was 65 cases' worth of body before + new). tools/prove-gates.py (scope widened by the orchestrator): one red row job_cap_drift on .github/workflows/ci.yml, kind 'after', anchor '    name: resample (windows)
', payload a strategy/matrix 'draw: [1..21]' -> expected red jc0; two allow rows on tools/gate-parity.py: '        if row["count"] <= cap:' -> '< cap' (expected red jc2), and '        alone = [job for job in on
' -> '... on if False
' (gate job counted; expected red jc2). Each anchor occurs exactly once (grep -c: 1, 1, 1). Mutation probe output, `python3 tools/prove-gates.py --only job_cap` exit 0: 'job_cap_drift RED jc0, jc3' / '1 of 1 gates proven red'; allow 'job_cap_drift RED jc2, jc3' and 'job_cap_drift RED jc0, jc1, jc2, jc3' / '2 of 2 guards proven to stay quiet on known-good input'. prove-gates --list shows the three rows 'anchored'; prove-gates --selftest ALL PASS 65/65 (baseline before the change: 65/65). .github/workflows/ci.yml: the lint-job comment's 'Nothing checks the job count against the cap' replaced by what now checks it (job_cap_drift, JOB_CAP, jc0 prints the counts, one run counted). Measured over the live ci.yml with the linux `parts` row raised and its excludes removed: linux 3 parts -> per-run 18 / release 19, no finding (the finding's 20/21 was before P151.3 cut the windows code-page leg to 3 parts, leaving 12 cells); linux 4 -> 20/21, release tier reported; linux 5 -> 22/23, both tiers reported; shard_matrix_drift [] in all three, so only job_cap_drift sees it. Dependants: ci.yml's 37 path-dependants (audit-task.py, tests/_harness.py, test__impact, test__manifest_phases, test__refs, test_audit_task, test_drive_phase, tools/affected.py) reference the path or fixtures of their own, not the comment text changed - still correct; test__refs, test__impact, test__manifest_phases, affected.py selftests pass. gate-parity.py's dependants: no existing function, signature or name changed (floating_runners, image_in_job_names, job_bound_evidence, launcher_contract untouched); parity() gained a key, render() reads it - its only callers are main() and its own cases; sweep-costs.json, _areas.py, bench-hooks.py, _output_lints.py, measure-affected-miss.py, test_audit_task.py unaffected (bench-hooks, output_lints suites pass; test_audit_task/test_drive_phase only name the path in fixtures - not run, too slow, nothing they read changed).
outcome.descriptive: gate-parity now counts the jobs each CI tier's run starts at once against a named JOB_CAP of 20 and fails the build on a tier over it, proven both directions by prove-gates rows.
